# Load the spreadsheet
file_path = '/mnt/data/spreadsheet/50768/1_50768_init.xlsx'
df = pd.read_excel(file_path, header=None)

# Convert the entire dataframe to object type to avoid dtype warnings when inserting strings
df = df.astype(object)

# Extract the data starting from row 2 (index 2)
data_rows = df.iloc[2:].copy()
data_rows = data_rows.iloc[:, 0:3]
data_rows.columns = ['ID', 'Impact', 'Likelihood']

# Drop rows where any of the critical values are NaN
data_rows = data_rows.dropna(subset=['ID', 'Impact', 'Likelihood'])

# Initialize the matrix mapping
# F12:H14
# Rows: 12 (L=3), 13 (L=2), 14 (L=1)
# Cols: F (I=1), G (I=2), H (I=3)
matrix = {
    (11, 5): [], (11, 6): [], (11, 7): [], # Row 12 (index 11), Likelihood 3
    (12, 5): [], (12, 6): [], (12, 7): [], # Row 13 (index 12), Likelihood 2
    (13, 5): [], (13, 6): [], (13, 7): []  # Row 14 (index 13), Likelihood 1
}

for _, row in data_rows.iterrows():
    try:
        # Use float then int to handle potential float strings like '1.0'
        rid = str(int(float(row['ID'])))
        impact = int(float(row['Impact']))
        likelihood = int(float(row['Likelihood']))
        
        # Map Likelihood to row index: 3->11, 2->12, 1->13
        row_idx = 14 - likelihood 
        # Map Impact to col index: 1->5, 2->6, 3->7
        col_idx = 4 + impact
        
        if (row_idx, col_idx) in matrix:
            matrix[(row_idx, col_idx)].append(rid)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        continue

# Write the results back to the original dataframe
for (r, c), ids in matrix.items():
    df.iloc[r, c] = ", ".join(ids)

# Save to output path
output_path = '/mnt/data/outputs/50768_0_d138c375/1_50768_output.xlsx'
df.to_excel(output_path, index=False, header=False)",
